sources.quote: In 2025, the House Rules Committee—controlled by the speaker—prohibited consideration of any amendments on about 84% of the measures it sent to the floor, the data shows.
sources.searcher_note: BGov data analysis of House rules: 95 closed rules in 2025, ~80% of submitted amendments blocked vs 54-68% in prior Congresses; measures closed rules, not amendment roll calls per bill passed.

sources.quote: A report compiled by committee Democrats shows that the GOP made zero amendments in order for 95 separate pieces of legislation throughout the first year of the 119th Congress
sources.searcher_note: Record-setting Congress piece; also carries GOP pushback: 25 of the 95 were Congressional Review Act measures, not amendable, and members offered no amendments for 20.

sources.quote: For instance, the spokesperson said, of the 95 pieces of legislation the Democrats invoke, 25 were Congressional Review Act measures, which are not amendable.
sources.searcher_note: Disagreement/nuance on the same page: Rules Republicans say many closed measures could not be amended anyway.

sources.outlet: House Rules Committee Democrats (Ranking Member McGovern)
sources.quote: Today, Republicans officially broke their own record for the most measures ever advanced to the floor with no amendments allowed.
sources.searcher_note: Minority release: 117 closed rules since January 2025, called the most closed Congress in history (partisan source).

sources.quote: More than 8 out of every 10 rules issued this Congress have locked down debate and allowed zero amendments on the floor.
sources.searcher_note: One-page summary of the December 2025 Democratic staff report; closed-rule share and amendments blocked, first year of 119th Congress.

sources.quote: more than half of the closed measures were closed by definition—meaning there were no amendments that could even be made in order.
sources.searcher_note: Majority rebuttal: of 95 closed rules in 2025 only 33 percent were closed at the committee's discretion (CRAs, rules-package bills, bills with no amendments filed).

notes: Every source found measures the same House/119th Congress but with a different yardstick: closed rules and share of submitted amendments blocked. None counts amendment roll call votes, none gives the share of roll-call-passed bills that drew an amendment roll call, and none uses a 1995-2024 baseline or the 12%/61% figures. Rules Republicans dispute the closed-rule framing (CRAs not amendable, no amendments filed). No coverage dated after 2026-06-30 on this measure was found (an MS NOW opinion of 2026-09-18 on the House recess did not mention amendments). Two queries (#4, #7) triggered the search tool's own internal follow-up searches, so actual web search consumption was higher than 8.
